mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative despite sustained FEDFUNDS > 4% for 6 months, or the IC > 0.05 over a 12-month horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate > 0.5% AND UNRATE < 4% over the preceding 2 months
failure_condition: IC < -0.1 over 60-day window despite strong labor indicators, or SPX 60d returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from supply-side to demand-side constraints, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 10% in a single month while INDPRO falls by > 5% from the prior month
failure_condition: 20 consecutive 5-day periods show no negative returns when demand is high and supply is weak (IC > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing production (INDPRO) below trend suggests supply-side contraction, lowering equity valuations and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: IC > 0.1 over 20-day horizon or 20d returns are positive when INDPRO is in contraction phase.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2% for the first time in a rising trend, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% and shows a positive monthly trend
failure_condition: 20d returns remain negative despite CPIAUCSL > 2% for 3 consecutive months (IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) without a corresponding decline in employment (PAYEMS) suggests labor market weakness that depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month for 4 consecutive months
regime_hint: rising unemployment benefits without employment decline
failure_condition: IC < -0.2 over 60-day window or 60d returns are positive when PAYEMS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer (HOUST) and industrial demand (RSAFS) above their 12-month averages creates optimism about future growth, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: IC > 0.15 when both proxies are above trend, or 20d returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime of declining industrial production (INDPRO) combined with a sustained decline in consumer confidence proxies (not available in evidence - use alternative) — instead, here: a long-term downward trend in GDP deflator inflation proxies (not available) — so instead, use supply via RSAFS: A multi-year decline in RSAFS (supply chain activity) predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as valuations adjust for supply constraints.
failure_condition: IC < -0.2 over 60-day horizon or 60d returns are positive during sustained supply contraction.
